walkthroughs.body_html:
Exponentials & Logarithms — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Exponentials & Logarithms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Exponentials & Logarithms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which average is best to use for the data set [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 100]?
options: The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.
The median (3.5) — it isn't distorted by the outlier 100, unlike the mean.
The mean — it always gives the most accurate average.
20 and 30, by treating 2 : 3 as the actual amounts.

mcqs.q: In a school the ratio of boys to girls is 3:2. There are 30 boys. How many girls are there?
options: 20 — each part of the ratio represents 10 pupils, so girls = 2 x 10.
There are 60 girls because girls are double the boys.
There are 27 girls because the ratio 3:2 means subtracting 3 - 2 = 1 from 30 and adding to make 2 girls' part.
20 and 30, by treating 2 : 3 as the actual amounts.
24 and 36 — 5 parts in total, each part is 12, so 2 x 12 = 24 and 3 x 12 = 36.
30 and 30, by splitting 60 in half because there are two numbers in the ratio.
20 and 30, by treating 2 : 3 as the actual amounts.
The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.
